No fine follows, however, because the upfront fare already puts the distance-and-time economics on your side. The deviation is established but not material: 6.15 km and 29.71% are below both material limbs (8.0 km and 50% of optimal), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged by materiality; on its named fields driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d (ratio 0.00, below the 0.05 threshold), so no repeat pattern exists and no conduct referral follows. ruling.explanation:
For both parties: the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee cannot stand and is refunded in full to the rider.

Trip TRP-00703 was a 05:30 STANDARD-zone pickup in a RYDE_PLUS vehicle. The rider cancelled at 05:34:00. Under POL-NS-01 the fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold, and each fails. (a) The trip record carries no driver 'arrived' event: arrived_at, started_at and ended_at are all null. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00703) holds 25 fixes at a 10-second cadence from 05:30:00 to 05:34:00 with 100% coverage and no gaps, and every fix places the driver between 19,176 m and 19,330 m from the pickup pin — against a 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — so the derived arrival block returns 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes. (c) The longest qualifying in-geofence run was 0.0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum. (d) The trip was cancelled by the rider (status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER, cancelled_by RIDER), not terminated by the driver with one of the recognised reason codes.

POL-NS-02 then applies on its own terms: where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes before cancellation, the driver never arrived and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. POL-NS-06 reaches the same result independently — the effective in-geofence dwell of 0 seconds is 300 seconds short of the required minimum — and the fee is refunded whether or not the rider was present or responded to messages.

The driver's own statement, 'I overslept and had not reached the pickup when she cancelled,' is an admission against his own interest and agrees with the telemetry; it carries no weight multiplier, so it does not enter the confidence cap, but it confirms the ~19 km standoff and removes any suggestion that a real arrival was mis-recorded. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) is not in play: its test is a 400 m ceiling from the pin and the driver was roughly 19 km away.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not, and POL-NS-06 directs that no compensation is payable on a dwell shortfall; the SGD 4.80 'driver_compensation' figure in the fare breakdown's derived block therefore has no clause behind it on these facts. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip in any event: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against a threshold of 4, and 1 of 110 completed trips is 0.9 percent against the 0.08 rate limb.

POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) is not engaged and produces no referral: with no 'arrived' event at all there is no marker capable of being false. No traffic advisory exists for this pickup road (EV-ADVIS-00703-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), so the POL-NS-06(i) dwell-accumulation route is unavailable — but it is irrelevant, because the driver never entered the geofence for the dwell to be accumulated. POL-NS-04 is neither needed nor satisfied: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00703) is empty (0 messages) and the trace carries no rider track, so limb (a) cannot be run; the refund follows from the driver's side of the arrival test alone, before any question of the rider's own conduct arises.

No escalation arises under POL-NS-09: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, the same-party repeat limb is not engaged (both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0), no abuse pattern is shown, and every artifact carrying a deciding fact is at full weight 1.0.

The only amount in issue is the single SGD 6.00 cancellation-fee line in EV-FARE-00703 (payment status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). That figure is exactly the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee (SGD 6.00) under the fee_schedule resolution rule, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and no booking or platform fee is charged on a cancelled trip. The whole of that line — SGD 6.00 — is refunded.

Both parties: the contested SGD 9.40 is not a no-show or cancellation charge. EV-FARE-00705 (weight 1.0, COMPLETE) records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 9.40 and total_charged 9.40, itemised as base fare 3.80 + distance fare 2.45 + time fare 2.35 + platform fee 0.80, with the cancellation-fee line at 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED. EV-TRIP-00705 (weight 1.0, COMPLETE) shows status COMPLETED on a 2.3 km, 12.0-minute ride to the rider's registered home waypoint, with cancellation_reason_code, cancelled_at and cancelled_by all null. The no-show mechanism therefore never engaged and no cancellation fee was ever charged.

The rider is correct on the no-show arithmetic, and it decides nothing here. POL-NS-01 limb (d) fails because the trip was never terminated on RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and the in-geofence dwell was only 50 seconds (6 qualifying fixes, 12:12:50 to 12:13:40) against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 250-second shortfall under POL-NS-06. But those findings decide whether a cancellation fee is chargeable, and the cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00 - POL-NS-06 refunds that line, and refunding zero is nothing. The rider's request is not for that line; it is for the completed-trip fare, and no no-show clause makes a delivered, correctly-priced ride refundable. POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00705-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0); that absence does not change the outcome.

The driver is also correct that the compensation machinery pays out nothing: POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not, and 80 percent of a SGD 0.00 fee line is SGD 0.00. The anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 110). No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged - confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, no repeat-party counters read anything, and the deciding facts are carried by full-weight (1.0) artifacts under POL-GEN-02(2). No referral is produced by any clause: there are qualifying in-geofence fixes, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire, and no other referral clause applies.

The rider's cash-demand allegation is not supported by the record: EV-CHAT-00705 contains zero messages, EV-TRIP-00705 records chat_message_count 0 and no in-app calls, the driver's statement of 2026-09-23 denies collecting anything beyond the platform-calculated fare, and the rider herself concedes that no separate cash waiting payment was made. That allegation cannot be verified on this record, but it does not make the platform fare refundable.

Result: the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence, and the present state stands. The SGD 9.40 charge is left in place; no refund and no driver compensation issue.

Both parties: the SGD 14.20 in dispute is the fare of a completed trip, not a no-show or cancellation fee, so there is nothing in this category to refund. The payments ledger itemises the SGD 14.20 as base fare SGD 3.80 + distance fare SGD 6.05 + time fare SGD 3.55 + platform fee SGD 0.80, and its cancellation-fee line is SGD 0.00. The trip record shows a COMPLETED trip (started 11:13:40, ended 11:26:40, 5.8 km in 13.0 min, against an optimal 6.0 km, a deviation of -3.3%) with cancelled_at, cancelled_by and cancellation_reason_code all null, so POL-NS-01 limb (d) is not met and no no-show fee was ever chargeable. Every refund route in the category — POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 — operates only on the cancellation-fee line, which is SGD 0.00, so none of them moves money, and POL-NS-07 driver compensation is unavailable because it presupposes POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, which this completed trip does not satisfy. The rider's account of the trip is substantially borne out: he walked to the car (the driver's closest approach to the pin was 298.04 m, so he never entered the 50 m STANDARD geofence), the trip ended early under the LTA CLOSURE advisory on the Canal-side access road (active 10:43:40 to 11:56:40, overlapping the trip by 13.0 minutes), and the driver wrote 'Water too deep; I will end here' at 11:24:50. That is a genuine service/route complaint, but it lies outside the NO_SHOW_CHARGE category, and these clauses can refund only a cancellation fee, not a completed-trip fare. To the driver: no fee and no compensation arise, and the fare as charged is supported by the distance and time actually driven.

I reject the rider's fare-integrity argument. The contention that POL-NS-08(d) is engaged because the ledger's cancellation-fee line (SGD 0.00) differs from the SGD 4.00 that fee_schedule.resolution_rule produces for a STANDARD pickup and a RYDE_X vehicle (the ledger's own derived 'difference' of -4.00) does not hold: the resolution-rule figure is the amount of a chargeable cancellation fee, no cancellation fee was chargeable on this completed trip, and the SGD 0.00 line is therefore correct and reconciles. There is no fare defect, no impairment to cap confidence, and no POL-NS-09(e) escalation. No other escalation trigger fires either: the records agree on arrival, dwell and completion, so POL-NS-09(b) is not engaged, and the profile checks show driver no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against completed_trips_30d of 110 (rate 0.009), with no_show_disputes_30d and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 on both sides, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged. Rating, account-age and lifetime fields are context only (POL-GEN-01) and were given no weight. The present state therefore stands and the disputed charge is left as it is; if the rider wishes to pursue the early-termination complaint, that must be raised outside the no-show category.

To the rider and the driver: this case is decided by the waiting-time arithmetic, not by conduct. The driver genuinely arrived. The 'arrived' event is at 13:12:40, and the GPS trace puts him stationary at the pin throughout — all 25 fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, mean distance 2.32 m, maximum 3.71 m, constant 0.0 km/h — so POL-NS-02 is satisfied, limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met on the driver's side, and I accept the driver's points that this is a real arrival at the pin and that the marker was not false: the 10 second event-to-fix offset is well inside the 90 second skew tolerance and neither POL-NS-05 trigger (over 300 m, or at or above 15 km/h) engages. But POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and the dwell fails. Measured as POL-NS-01(c) directs — from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 13:12:50, not from the 'arrived' tap, to the rider's cancellation at 13:16:50 — the driver held position for 240 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum, a 60 second shortfall. Limb (d) also fails: the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER at 13:16:50, not a driver termination on one of the recognised reason codes. The fee is therefore not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and POL-NS-06 is decisive: where the effective in-geofence dwell is below the minimum for the zone class, the cancellation fee is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The only way to reach 300 seconds was to sum separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i), which requires a traffic advisory that is present and populated; EV-ADVIS-00706-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and can carry no fact, so that route is closed and the shortfall stands. The refund is the cancellation-fee line only: SGD 4.00, which is the whole contested amount and reconciles with fee_schedule (STANDARD zone-class fee 4.00 and RYDE_POOL vehicle-tier fee 4.00 — the greater is 4.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect). No driver compensation attaches: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-06 says in terms that a shortfall carries none. The driver's chat request to 'wait for a match' because 'the base fare is too low' (13:13:20) and his statement that he asked her to wait are noted, and the rider's account that the doors stayed locked is consistent with them, but no clause in this category converts that, or the locked doors, into money in either direction, so it does not change the refund. I also address the rider's POL-NS-04 claim: her 13:14:00 message 'I stopped matching. Please unlock and go.' is a demand to proceed, not the locating or coordinating content limb (a) lists (her own position, an entrance/block/tower/bay, a request for the driver's position, or a statement she cannot see the vehicle), so that clause is not open to her — it makes no difference, because POL-NS-06 already gives the full refund. The driver's points that this is not a wrong-entrance or circling case and that no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises (registered_pickup_points is 1) are accepted. No referral is produced: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because the arrival marker was not false, and no other clause adds one. No escalation: the artifacts carrying the deciding dwell and fee facts — trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown — are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0, the trace has 25 fixes and no gaps, the rider track is present, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, and the fare reconciles, so nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d); the profiles show 0 disputes between these parties and 0 rider no-show disputes in 30 days, and the driver's anti-farming counters (1 termination against 110 completed trips) do not trip POL-NS-07 or POL-NS-09(d). Confidence 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by those weight-1.0 artifacts.

To both parties: this complaint was filed through the no-show channel, but the record shows a completed trip, and the SGD 15.60 in dispute is the metered fare for that trip — not a no-show or cancellation charge. The rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS. EV-TRIP-00707 records status COMPLETED, accepted_at and arrived_at 2026-09-23T14:12:40, started_at 14:13:40, ended_at 14:26:40, with cancelled_at, cancelled_by and cancellation_reason_code all null. EV-GPS-00707 shows the vehicle covering the full 5.5 km route over that window (84 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps). EV-FARE-00707 itemises the SGD 15.60 as base fare SGD 3.80 + distance fare SGD 7.10 + time fare SGD 3.90 + platform fee SGD 0.80 = SGD 15.60; its cancellation_fee line is SGD 0.00, refund_issued_sgd is SGD 0.00, and the ledger's own money block reports fee_charged SGD 0.00. The driver's statement ('the ride completed normally; no cancellation fee was charged') agrees with the instruments.

WHY THE NO-SHOW FRAMEWORK DECIDES NOTHING HERE. POL-NS-01 makes a cancellation fee chargeable only where all four limbs hold — limb (d) among them, requiring the trip to be terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. No such termination occurred. The rider advocate's points that limb (d) and limb (b) fail, and that the dwell is short (longest qualifying in-geofence run 50 s against the 300 s STANDARD minimum, shortfall 250 s), are correct as far as they go — but they concern a cancellation fee, and SGD 0.00 of cancellation fee was ever charged. POL-NS-02 through POL-NS-06 refund 'the cancellation-fee line only, not any booking or platform fee that would have been charged on a completed trip', so there is nothing within this category for them to return.

THE RIDER ADVOCATE'S STEP FROM THOSE FACTS TO A FULL REFUND IS REJECTED. The dispute's category label (NO_SHOW_CHARGE) does not convert a metered fare into a no-show fee; the fare breakdown's own cancellation-fee and fee_charged lines are SGD 0.00, and the SGD 15.60 is the price of a ride the rider actually took. The rider advocate's POL-NS-04 and POL-NS-07 points are accepted (no rider track, so limb (c) is undecidable and neutral; no compensation can arise on an unsatisfied POL-NS-01), but neither produces money in the rider's favour.

THE RIDER'S STATED GROUNDS. A smell in the vehicle and no help with a suitcase are service-quality complaints about a trip that was performed. No clause of POLICY-NO-SHOW licenses a refund of a completed-trip metered fare on those grounds. This ruling does not reach their merits; they remain open to the rider through the platform's service-quality channel.

OTHER POINTS. EV-ADVIS-00707-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING, weight 0.00, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence decides nothing here because no fee was charged, and POL-NS-06(i) is recorded unavailable on that ground. POL-NS-05(ii) produces no false-arrival referral because six qualifying in-geofence fixes exist. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d 0; both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0; the anti-farming check at no_show_terminations_30d 1 of 110 completed trips does not trip), so the case is not escalated and the fee is not held. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00 exactly as they are.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts — the trip completed and no cancellation fee was charged — are carried by EV-TRIP-00707, EV-FARE-00707 and EV-GPS-00707, each at weight 1.00, so the cap is 1.00; confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To the driver and to the rider: this dispute is decided on the fare record and the GPS trace, and it leaves both of you where you already are.

The driver's request — that the SGD 3.00 ERP line be released to him — cannot be granted. The SGD 3.00 is the 'Canal Corridor entry' charge. The fare breakdown records it as on the optimal route, and the GPS trace passes the gantry at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m at 16:24:40, so it is a real crossing of a real on-route gantry, properly chargeable as a government pass-through under POL-RD-09. No clause turns an ERP pass-through into a payment to the driver: POL-RD-04 driver compensation requires the rider to have been billed for more than 1.0 km less than the trace records, and here the ledger bills 11.0 km against an 11.0 km trace — no shortfall — while POL-RD-12 applies only to RYDE_POOL trips and this was a RYDE_X trip. POL-RD-11(a) fixes an UPFRONT_QUOTE rider's remedy at charged_total 26.00 less quoted_fare 23.00 less the properly chargeable pass-through of 3.00, which is exactly the 0.00 the ledger publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy: nothing is owing from this fare to either party.

There is likewise no deviation to refund to the rider or to charge to the driver. The governing trace figure is 11.0 km under POL-RD-01, against an optimal of 11.2 km — an excess of -0.2 km, or -1.8%. Both establishment tests fail (the excess must exceed 0.8 km and 20% of optimal), and re-running the test on the amended endpoints under POL-RD-05 gives the same amended optimal of 11.2 km / 20.0 min and the same negative excess, so POL-RD-05's own direction is NO_ACTION. The destination amendment is timestamped 16:27:40, after the gantry was charged at 16:24:40, so it neither created nor removed the ERP line.

The rider's point that the amended baseline leaves the gantry unverified is rejected: the trace crossed the gantry on the route as actually driven at 16:24:40, before the amendment, and the line is flagged on the optimal route. There is no traffic advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-00709-01 is missing, weight 0.0), and because no party asserts an external traffic cause, POL-RD-03 has no advisory to run against and plays no part.

The outcome is NO_ACTION: the fare stands, payment_status remains PENDING and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, left exactly as they are. No money moves to either party, and no referral is produced — there is no material deviation and no repeat-pattern finding for a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral, and no phantom or off-route line for a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider: I have considered your point that the pool booking said the ERP was shared and that another rider was aboard. The contested SGD 6.00 is the only ERP line on the bill. Your trip was an upfront quote of SGD 25.00 (base SGD 3.80 + distance SGD 14.15 + time SGD 6.25 + platform fee SGD 0.80 = SGD 25.00 exactly), and the charged total was SGD 31.00, the extra being the SGD 6.00 ERP pass-through. Under POL-RD-11 an upfront-quoted, quoted_fare 25.00 trip gives no distance-or-time refund, so the only question is whether the SGD 6.00 ERP line is properly chargeable. It is. The single gantry ('Matched itinerary gantry') lies on the matched-itinerary optimal route, and the GPS trace passes it: the nearest fix is 0.0 m from the gantry coordinates at 07:30:40, inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) applies. That makes it a crossed, on-route gantry, not a phantom line, so no billing-integrity refund arises and the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic is charged_total 31.00 - quoted_fare 25.00 - properly chargeable ERP 6.00 = 0.00. Your argument that the gantry coordinates sit only on the ledger that bills them does not change this: POL-RD-09(4) prescribes exactly that comparison, and the trace independently places a fix at the gantry at the charged instant. Your request for a pro-rata share fails for a separate reason - the policy contains no mechanism to split a metered ERP pass-through between co-riders. POL-RD-12 (pooled trips) adjusts only the distance baseline and does not touch ERP, and no booking-terms artifact showing a shared-ERP term exists in the bundle; the only source for that term is your own message. I also cannot find a distance deviation: the governing trace figure is 11.99 km against the matched-itinerary optimal of 12.2 km, an excess of -0.21 km (-1.72%), which fails both POL-RD-01 tests, and the 8.5 km solo optimal is not the baseline for a RYDE_POOL trip. Your fallback request for ESCALATE is declined: no POL-RD-10 trigger fires (see below). To the driver: the ERP line stands as charged, and your statement that the gantry was crossed on the matched itinerary is corroborated by the trace. Your chat message 'Pay the full ERP on this booking' does not affect the outcome - the line is chargeable because the trace crossed an on-route gantry, not because you demanded payment. No POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour is in play (the chat contains no instruction, and no waypoint), and no POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: there is no material deviation and no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250). On escalation, POL-RD-10 is not engaged: the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s sampling), the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and ledger, no refund computation exceeds any ceiling, and the ERP line has its counterpart in the trace. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00710-01, weight 0.0) is neutral, since neither party asserted an external traffic cause; and the ledger's note that the gantry match radius is not a structured field is a data-modelling note, not a finding that the match is undecidable - POL-RD-09(4) supplies the test and the record satisfies it. Result: the charge stands. payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00. Confidence 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding fact (the GPS trace and the fare breakdown).

To the rider: the factual core of your account is supported. The driver's own statement concedes the passengers never boarded ('the passengers were confused and walked away'), and your 15:16:50 in-app message ('My parents are still at the pickup. Did anyone board?') is consistent with it.
